page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g9a.32xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by AMD EPYC 9T25 x86_64 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz, delivering 128 dedicated vCPUs. The hardware configuration couples these dedicated compute cores with 512.0 GB of system memory, establishing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU core.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, necessitating remote cloud storage for filesystem and operational data. It is equipped with a baseline network bandwidth of 64 Gbps and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Dedicated graphics accelerators are not present in this configuration, making it strictly a central processing and memory compute node.

With 128 dedicated execution cores and 512.0 GB of memory backed by high-throughput 64 Gbps networking, the instance suits parallel computing needs without incurring specialized accelerator costs. The resource profile aligns with enterprise application servers, large-scale microservice deployments, continuous integration systems, data batch processing, and distributed database backends.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g9a.32xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance powered by AMD EPYC 9T25 processors running at 2.7 GHz on a KVM hypervisor. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs and 512.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 allocation ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The configuration does not include local storage disks or hardware accelerator GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached block storage for persistent data requirements. Network performance is provisioned with a 64 Gbps baseline bandwidth, though complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included. The balance of 128 dedicated execution threads, substantial memory footprint, and high-throughput network connectivity suits resource-demanding enterprise deployments. Typical target workloads comprise large-scale web application clusters, enterprise resource planning systems, batch data processing pipelines, distributed databases, continuous integration build clusters, and dense containerized microservices requiring consistent compute and memory resources.
